title: OpenAI invoke proxy: sideloaded tool manifests and framing v3
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds optional sideloaded tool manifests and improved stream framing (v3) to the OpenAI compatibility proxy. Opt-in via header or per-tenant config. Backwards compatible; includes manifest signature verification and new telemetry for tool-invoke reliability.
body:
Context and motivation: Several customers reported flaky tool/function calls when the model emitted mid-stream tool metadata that did not match the canonical registry (race between model-provided schema and server-side canonicalization). This PR introduces an opt-in sideloaded tool manifest flow and a more robust stream framing protocol (framing v3) to make OpenAI-compat invoke behavior deterministic across fragmented streams. The intent is to reduce schema mismatch fallbacks and improve reassembly stability for streaming tool invocation while keeping legacy behavior unchanged unless explicitly enabled.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a sideloaded manifest mechanism: requests can include a pre-provided tool manifest payload (or reference) carried in a new header X-OpenAI-Compat-ToolManifest or via multipart sideload. The proxy will prefer the sideloaded manifest for schema mapping and will fall back to registry lookup if verification fails.
- Implements manifest signature verification and strict provenance checks (manifest/issuer/digest) to guard against tampered tool descriptors.
- Introduces framing v3 for OpenAI-compat streams: per-fragment checksums, explicit envelope delimiters with escape handling, and ACK/HEARTBEAT pair for long-lived streams to avoid silent partial-merge bugs.
- Enhances tool_choice semantics: when sideloaded manifests are present, the proxy uses manifest-qualified tool IDs during deterministic tiebreaking (reduces ambiguity between forks of the same logical tool).
- Adds opt-in toggles: tenant_config.allow_sideload (console flag) and request-level header X-OpenAI-Compat-Allow-Sideload=true.
- Backwards compatible: if neither header nor tenant toggle is set, proxy behaves the same as before. Framing v3 is negotiated on the stream (Accept-Framing: v3) so older clients are unaffected.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for manifest parsing and verification, [x] integration test with model-fragmented tool invocation, [x] e2e with sample sideloaded manifest from console example, [x] docs and migration notes, [x] telemetry hooks.

Files/areas touched (high level): proxy/openai_compat/manifest/sideload.go, proxy/openai_compat/manifest/verify.go, proxy/openai_compat/framing/v3.go, proxy/openai_compat/handler_invoke.go (routing changes), proxy/openai_compat/test/e2e_sideload_test.go, docs/openai-tool-sideload.md, console/examples/tool-sideloading.js, sdk/python/openai_compat.py (helper), observability/metrics/tool_invoke_metrics.go, CI config to expose e2e cluster with streaming node.

Commits: condensed list below (full history in commit log). The important logical steps are: add sideload transport, implement verification, add framing v3 encoder/decoder, wire into invoke path, tests, docs.

Testing and CI: Unit and integration test suite was updated. Integration tests flapped once on stream reassembly; I added a deterministic buffer flush in the encoder and retried; CI passed on rerun. The e2e uses the staging model that simulates fragmented function call outputs.

Rollout plan: Feature flagged by tenant. Default is opt-out. We'll enable for three beta customers (noted in ENG-3412) for 2 weeks and monitor the following signals: tool_invoke_failures, tool_schema_mismatch_rate, stream_fragment_reassembly_latency, api_error_rate. If regressions are observed we will roll back by tenant toggle.

Migration notes: If you rely on model-provided schema inference to pick between multiple tool variants with identical names, enabling sideloaded manifests will bias toward the manifest canonicalization. If you need the old behavior, keep tenant toggle disabled. SDK helper updated to attach manifest as multipart sideload for Python/TS examples.

Security notes: Manifest verification is required when the tenant flag tenant_config.require_signed_manifest=true. By default we accept unsigned manifests but will log a high-severity telemetry event to aid auditing during the beta.

Related tickets and design docs: ENG-3412 (design), ENG-3550 (telemetry), SUP-812 (customer report). Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3412/openai-sideloaded-manifests-and-framing-v3 (internal).

Merge: squash merge after approvals.
commits: add: sideload manifest transport and parsing (proxy/openai_compat/manifest)
feat: framing v3 encoder/decoder with fragment checksum and ack protocol
feat: manifest signature verification and provenance checks
fix: deterministic buffer flush to stabilize streaming e2e tests
test: add e2e for fragmented tool invocation using sideload
review_comments: Liam Carter: Can we avoid accepting unsigned manifests by default? Reply (Priya): opt-in default reduces blast radius for early beta; we added tenant_config.require_signed_manifest for customers that want strictness.

Sofia Martinez: Framing v3 adds overhead — did you benchmark latency at 95th percentile? Reply (Priya): yes, added perf note in design doc; overhead is ~0.6ms median on 8K tokens but reduces reassembly retries which improves 95th overall.

Ethan Zhao: Please add an integration test that simulates partial fragment duplication. Reply (Priya): added e2e test e2e_sideload_test.go that duplicates a fragment and verifies idempotent coalescing.
QA (Riley): flake observed on CI - reran jobs and added deterministic flush to encoder to address race.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (rerun once due to flake)
